Why it drew attention

Points and comments measure interest at one moment; they do not verify the linked article or settle the debate.

Distinguish statements in the original article from interpretations added in the comment thread.

Read it in this order

Open the linked source first and note its evidence. Then read the Hacker News comments for counterexamples, corrections, and additional references. Recheck any important conclusion against a primary source.

Bottom line

  • Comments at collection: 118 — official record
  • Points at collection: 377 — official record
  • Author: paulirish — official record
  • Discussion text: Browsers natively handle a lot of what used to take 50 lines of JS (or a dependency): `CSS.highlights` for text range highlighting without <span>s everywhere, `<dialog>` and showModal() give you backdrops and ideal focus management, `field-sizing` to auto-grow textareas as the user types.. (Something yesterday's ftrain post touched on [0]) Models know about some of these by name, but consistently won't default to using the platform-native solution and instead prefer the incumbent <div>+JS based pattern. We started an effort in Chrome to supplement coding agents with this key domain knowledge and we're shipping our 1.0 today, in collaboration with Firefox, MDN, and Edge. 200+ guides (~1.7MB) — official record
